## Content parts

The content of a message can be a list of parts. Each part is a dict
with a `type`. `mk_content(o)` builds one part. The result depends on
the input:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>input</th>
<th>result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>a string</td>
<td>a text part</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>bytes or a path, holding an image</td>
<td>an <code>image_url</code> part with the picture embedded as a base64
data URL</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>bytes or a path, holding audio</td>
<td>an <code>input_audio</code> part</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>a dict</td>
<td>the dict, unchanged. Urai assumes it is a part already.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>any other bytes or path, such as a PDF</td>
<td><code>TypeError</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>any other type</td>
<td><code>TypeError</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

[`mk_content`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#mk_content)
reads the bytes of a path and inspects them to find the type. The
`TypeError` reports an attachment that the model cannot read. Urai never
drops it silently.

`is_media(p)` returns `True` when a part is an image part or an audio
part.

### mk_content

``` python
def mk_content(
    o
):
```

*Convert `o` to an OpenAI-style content part: text, a base64
`image_url`, or an `input_audio`.*

``` python
test_eq(mk_content('hi'), {'type': 'text', 'text': 'hi'})
test_eq(mk_content({'type': 'text', 'text': 'passthrough'}), {'type': 'text', 'text': 'passthrough'})
test_eq(mk_content(tiny_png)['type'], 'image_url')
assert mk_content(tiny_png)['image_url']['url'].startswith('data:image/png;base64,')
test_eq(mk_content(tiny_wav)['input_audio']['format'], 'wav')
```

``` python
test_fail(lambda: mk_content(b'%PDF-1.4 not media'), contains='text, image, and audio')
test_fail(lambda: mk_content(42), contains='Unsupported content type')
test_eq(is_media(mk_content(tiny_png)), True)
test_eq(is_media(mk_content('hi')), False)
test_eq(_audio_fmt('audio/mpeg'), 'mp3')
test_eq(_audio_fmt('audio/ogg'), 'ogg')     # unknown: the subtype is the best guess
```

## Messages

`mk_msg(content, role)` builds one message from a string, bytes, a path,
or a list that mixes these. A message dict is returned unchanged. `None`
is also returned unchanged. When every part is text,
[`mk_msg`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#mk_msg) joins
the parts with newlines into one string. A message with a part that is
not text keeps the list form. An image part is an example.
[`mk_msgs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#mk_msgs)
applies [`mk_msg`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#mk_msg)
to a list of messages.

``` python
test_eq(mk_msg('hi'), {'role': 'user', 'content': 'hi'})
test_eq(mk_msg(['a', 'b']), {'role': 'user', 'content': 'a\nb'})
```

``` python
m = mk_msg(['look:', tiny_png])
test_eq(m['role'], 'user')
test_eq([p['type'] for p in m['content']], ['text', 'image_url'])
test_eq(mk_msgs(['a', 'b']), [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'a'}, {'role': 'user', 'content': 'b'}])
test_eq(mk_msgs(None), [])
```

A picture in the history is sent again with every later turn. It costs
the same tokens each time. `strip_media(m)` replaces each media part in
a message with the placeholder `[image]` or `[audio]`. It joins the
content with newlines into one string. The history still records that a
picture was there. Call
[`strip_media`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#strip_media)
on past turns before you send them. `strip_hist_media(hist)` does the
same for a whole history. Use it to save a conversation to disk without
the base64 data.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/msgs.py#L74"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

## Tools

A tool schema is a JSON description of a tool. It gives the name, a
description, and the parameters. `mk_toolspec(f)` builds the schema from
a Python function with
[`fastcore.funccall.get_schema`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/funccall.html#get_schema).
`get_schema` reads the name of the function, its docstring, its type
annotations, and the comment after each parameter.

[`mk_toolspec`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#mk_toolspec)
returns a dict unchanged. Urai assumes the dict is a schema already. Use
a dict to describe a tool that the provider runs itself, such as a
hosted web search.

[`mk_toolspec`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#mk_toolspec)
handles two cases without the plain `get_schema` result. For a pydantic
model, it uses `model_json_schema`. It inlines each `$ref` and removes
the `title` keys. `get_schema` reads a pydantic model as one opaque
`data` field.

For a `Literal` annotation,
[`mk_toolspec`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#mk_toolspec)
writes an `enum` with the JSON type of the values. This holds for a
`Literal` alone and for a `Literal` inside `Optional`, a union or a
list. `get_schema` writes `"object[object, object]"` for these, which is
not a JSON Schema type. Strict providers such as Gemini refuse such a
schema.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/msgs.py#L121"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### lit_schema

``` python
def lit_schema(
    vals
):
```

*JSON Schema for a `Literal` of `vals`: their JSON type or types, and an
`enum` of them.*

``` python
def add(a: int,      # first addend
        b: int = 2   # second addend
       ) -> int:
    "Add two numbers."
    return a + b

spec = mk_toolspec(add)
test_eq(spec['type'], 'function')
test_eq(spec['function']['name'], 'add')
assert spec['function']['description'].startswith('Add two numbers.')
test_eq(sorted(spec['function']['parameters']['properties']), ['a', 'b'])
test_eq(mk_toolspec(spec), spec)
```

``` python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

class Color(enum.Enum): red = 'red'

@dataclass
class Pick:
    "A choice."
    a: Literal['x', 'y']
    b: Optional[Literal['p', 'q']] = None
    c: list[Literal['m', 'n']] = None
    d: Literal[1, True] = 1
    e: Literal[Color.red, None] = None

ps = mk_toolspec(Pick)['function']['parameters']['properties']
test_eq(ps['a'], {'description': '', 'type': 'string', 'enum': ['x', 'y']})
test_eq(ps['b']['anyOf'][0], {'type': 'string', 'enum': ['p', 'q']})
test_eq(ps['c']['items'], {'type': 'string', 'enum': ['m', 'n']})
test_eq(ps['d']['type'], ['integer', 'boolean'])
test_eq(ps['e']['enum'], ['red', None])
assert 'object[' not in json.dumps(ps)
```

``` python
class Outline:
    "Stands in for a pydantic model: what `model_json_schema` gives for one holding a list of another."
    @classmethod
    def model_json_schema(cls):
        return {'$defs': {'Part': {'title': 'Part', 'description': 'One part.', 'type': 'object', 'required': ['title'],
                                   'properties': {'title': {'title': 'Title', 'type': 'string'},
                                                  'kind': {'anyOf': [{'enum': ['a', 'b'], 'type': 'string'}, {'type': 'null'}], 'default': None, 'title': 'Kind'}}}},
                'title': 'Outline', 'description': 'An outline.', 'type': 'object', 'required': ['work', 'parts'],
                'properties': {'work': {'title': 'Work', 'type': 'string'},
                               'parts': {'title': 'Parts', 'type': 'array', 'items': {'$ref': '#/$defs/Part'}}}}

f = mk_toolspec(Outline)['function']
test_eq((f['name'], f['description']), ('Outline', 'An outline.'))
test_eq(sorted(f['parameters']['properties']), ['parts', 'work'])
test_eq(sorted(f['parameters']['properties']['parts']['items']['properties']), ['kind', 'title'])   # a field named `title` stays
assert '$ref' not in json.dumps(f) and '"title": "' not in json.dumps(f)
```

## Tool calls

When the model asks for a tool, the reply holds a list of tool calls.
`ToolCall(name, arguments)` builds one in the canonical form. It is a
`dict`, so code that indexes it as `tc['function']['name']` keeps
working, and it adds `name`, `arguments` and `server` properties for
easier reading. `server=True` marks a call the provider has already run
on its side, such as a hosted web search; the tool loop records such
calls but never runs them locally.

The other helpers work on plain dicts as well as
[`ToolCall`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#toolcall).
`tc_name(tc)` reads a call’s name, `tool_rows(m)` lists the
`(name, arguments)` of every call in a message, and
`mk_tool_res_msg(tc, result)` builds the `role='tool'` message that
sends a result back to the model, linked to the call by its id.
[`mk_tool_res_msgs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#mk_tool_res_msgs)
does that for several calls at once.

``` python
tc = ToolCall('add', {'a': 1})
test_eq((tc.name, tc.arguments, tc.server), ('add', {'a': 1}, False))
```

``` python
test_eq(mk_tool_res_msg(ToolCall('add', id='c1'), 3),
        {'role': 'tool', 'tool_call_id': 'c1', 'name': 'add', 'content': '3'})

test_eq(mk_tool_res_msgs([ToolCall('a')], []), [])     # zip stops at the shorter side
```

Most providers accept only text in a tool result message, so a tool
cannot hand back a screenshot directly. A tool that produces pictures
returns `ToolMedia(text, media)`, a string that also carries a list of
image paths or bytes. The text goes into the tool message as usual.
After all the results of a step, the tool loop sends the pictures to the
model in one extra user message. `tool_media(o)` returns the pictures a
result carries, or an empty list.

``` python
r = ToolMedia('saved shot.png', ['shot.png'])
test_eq((r, r.media, tool_media(r)), ('saved shot.png', ['shot.png'], ['shot.png']))
test_eq(mk_tool_res_msg(ToolCall('s', id='c1'), r)['content'], 'saved shot.png')
test_eq(type(mk_tool_res_msg(ToolCall('s'), r)['content']), str)
test_eq([tool_media('x'), tool_media(3), tool_media(ToolMedia('x'))], [[], [], []])
```

Small models often get argument types wrong. They write `"3"` where the
schema asks for an integer, `"true"` for a boolean, or a JSON string
where an object or a list belongs. Sometimes they nest all the arguments
one level down, under a key such as `arguments`.

`coerce_args(args, params)` converts each argument to the type its
schema declares: numbers, booleans (`true`, `yes`, `on` and their
opposites), strings, arrays (a single value becomes a one-item list) and
objects. The type always comes from the schema, never from how the value
looks, and a value that cannot be converted safely is left as the model
wrote it. Arguments without a declared type, or with a union type, are
not touched. `hoist_buried(args, params)` lifts missing required
parameters out of a nested container, but only when one container holds
all of them. `coerce_tcs(tcs, toolspecs)` applies both to every call in
a list, using each tool’s own schema found by
[`toolspec_params`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#toolspec_params),
and leaves calls to tools with no schema alone. The tool loop runs it on
each step.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/msgs.py#L240"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### toolspec_params

``` python
def toolspec_params(
    toolspecs, name
):
```

*The JSON schema `parameters` of tool `name` in `toolspecs`, or None
when no schema names it.*

``` python
p = mk_toolspec(add)['function']['parameters']
test_eq(coerce_args({'a': '1', 'b': 2}, p), {'a': 1, 'b': 2})    # the schema decides, not the spelling
test_eq(coerce_args({'a': 1, 'b': 2}, p), {'a': 1, 'b': 2})      # conforming args come back untouched
test_eq(coerce_args({'a': '1'}, p), coerce_args(coerce_args({'a': '1'}, p), p))   # idempotent
test_eq(coerce_args({'a': 1.5}, p), {'a': 1.5})   # not an integer and not roundable: left alone
test_eq(coerce_args({'a': 2.0}, p), {'a': 2})     # an integer spelled as a float is one
test_eq(coerce_args({'a': 'not a number'}, p), {'a': 'not a number'})   # an unparseable string is kept
```

``` python
flags = {'type': 'object', 'properties': {'ok': {'type': 'boolean'}, 'tags': {'type': 'array', 'items': {'type': 'string'}}},
         'required': ['ok']}
test_eq(coerce_args({'ok': 'true', 'tags': '[1, 2]'}, flags), {'ok': True, 'tags': ['1', '2']})
test_eq(coerce_args({'ok': 'maybe'}, flags), {'ok': 'maybe'})     # undecidable, so untouched

# a required param the model buried in a container is misplaced, not missing
test_eq(hoist_buried({'arguments': {'ok': True}}, flags), {'ok': True})
test_eq(hoist_buried({'arguments': {'nope': 1}}, flags), {'arguments': {'nope': 1}})   # no unanimity, no hoist

tcs = [ToolCall('add', {'a': '3'}), ToolCall('unknown', {'a': '3'})]
coerce_tcs(tcs, [mk_toolspec(add)])
test_eq(tcs[0]['function']['arguments'], {'a': 3})
test_eq(tcs[1]['function']['arguments'], {'a': '3'})   # no spec names it, so nothing is assumed
```

## In from the wire

`norm_resp(r)` converts a completion in the OpenAI response format into
a [`Resp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#resp), the urai
reply object. It does these steps:

- It moves `<think>` text into `channels['thought']`.
- It puts the native tool calls of the provider and the tagged calls in
  the text into one `tool_calls` list.
- It sets
  [`truncated`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#truncated)
  when the model stopped at the token limit.
- It keeps `usage`.

If the text has a tool block that
[`norm_resp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#norm_resp)
cannot parse, it sets `tool_parse_failed` on the reply. The tool loop
then asks the model to send the call again.

A provider sends native tool arguments as a JSON string.
[`parse_args`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#parse_args)
decodes the string. It returns a dict unchanged. It returns `None` for
empty strings, invalid JSON, or JSON values that are not objects. It
does not raise for these inputs.
[`norm_resp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/msgs.html#norm_resp)
marks these calls `unread` and sets `tool_parse_failed`. The loop can
ask for the call again. A valid `{}` remains readable.

`stream_resp(split, ...)` builds a
[`Resp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/core.html#resp) at the end
of a streamed step. Its inputs are a finished
[`StreamSplit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#streamsplit)
and the tool calls, thinking text and usage that the backend collected.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/msgs.py#L280"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

read.*

``` python
test_eq(parse_args('{"a": 1}'), {'a': 1})
test_eq(parse_args({'a': 1}), {'a': 1})
test_eq(parse_args(''), None)
test_eq(parse_args('{oops'), None)
_oai = lambda c: {'choices': [{'message': {'content': c}}]}
assert norm_resp(_oai('<tool_call>{"name": </tool_call>')).get('tool_parse_failed'), 'an unreadable call is lost without a word'
assert not norm_resp(_oai('<tool_call>{"name": "ls", "arguments": {}}</tool_call>')).get('tool_parse_failed')
```

Empty or invalid native arguments mark the call `unread`. A valid empty
JSON object stays readable.

``` python
for bad_args in ('', '{oops', '[]', 'null', None):
    assert parse_args(bad_args) is None, 'invalid native arguments must not become an empty dict'
    bad_native = norm_resp({'choices': [{'message': {'tool_calls': [
        {'id': 'bad', 'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': bad_args}}]}}]})
    assert bad_native['tool_calls'][0].get('unread')
    assert bad_native.get('tool_parse_failed')
test_eq(parse_args('{}'), {})
bad_native
```

``` python
r = norm_resp({'choices': [{'message': {'content': '<think>hmm</think>the answer'}}],
               'usage': {'total_tokens': 9}})
test_eq(r['content'], 'the answer')
test_eq(r['channels'], {'thought': 'hmm'})
test_eq(r['usage'], {'total_tokens': 9})
test_eq('tool_calls' in r, False)
test_eq(type(r), Resp)
```

``` python
r = norm_resp({'choices': [{'finish_reason': 'length', 'message': {
    'content': '', 'tool_calls': [{'id': 'c1', 'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': '{"a": 1}'}}]}}]})
test_eq(r['tool_calls'], [{'id': 'c1', 'type': 'function',
                           'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': {'a': 1}}}])
test_eq(r['truncated'], True)
```

``` python
r = norm_resp({'choices': [{'message': {
    'content': '<tool_call>{"name": "b", "arguments": {}}</tool_call>',
    'tool_calls': [{'id': 'c1', 'function': {'name': 'a', 'arguments': '{}'}}]}}]})
test_eq([t['function']['name'] for t in r['tool_calls']], ['a', 'b'])
```

## Out to the wire

History messages carry keys that providers reject, such as `channels`
and `usage`. `to_oai_msg(m)` converts a history message into a message
that an OpenAI-compatible API accepts.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Input</th>
<th>Result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>A key other than <code>role</code>, <code>content</code>,
<code>tool_calls</code>, <code>tool_call_id</code> or
<code>name</code></td>
<td>Dropped</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A key with the value <code>None</code></td>
<td>Dropped</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Tool call arguments that are a dict</td>
<td>Encoded as a JSON string</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A tool call with no <code>id</code></td>
<td><code>id</code> set to <code>call_</code> plus the position of the
call, such as <code>call_0</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A message with <code>tool_calls</code> and no
<code>content</code></td>
<td><code>content</code> set to <code>''</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Several providers refuse a message with tool calls and no `content`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/msgs.py#L293"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### to_oai_msg

``` python
def to_oai_msg(
    m
):
```

*Convert a history message to the form an OpenAI-compatible API
accepts.*

``` python
test_eq(to_oai_msg({'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'hi', 'channels': {'thought': 'x'},
                    'usage': {'total_tokens': 1}}),
        {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'hi'})
```

``` python
out = to_oai_msg({'role': 'assistant', 'tool_calls': [ToolCall('add', {'a': 1}, id='c1')]})
test_eq(out['content'], '')                            # providers reject a call turn with no content
test_eq(out['tool_calls'][0]['function']['arguments'], '{"a": 1}')
test_eq(to_oai_msg({'role': 'assistant', 'tool_calls': [{'function': {'name': 'f'}}]}
                   )['tool_calls'][0]['id'], 'call_0')
```

## Usage across rounds

A turn with tool calls takes several requests to the model. The first
request gets the calls. The next request follows the tool results.
`sum_usage(us)` adds the usage dicts of these requests and skips `None`.
It returns `None` when no request reported usage. The first `model` name
found in the dicts is kept.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key in the result</th>
<th>When it appears</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>prompt_tokens</code>, <code>completion_tokens</code>,
<code>total_tokens</code>, <code>cached_tokens</code></td>
<td>Always</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>reasoning_tokens</code>, <code>cache_creation_tokens</code>,
<code>cost</code></td>
<td>Only when the sum is not zero</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>model</code></td>
<td>Only when a usage dict names one</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The optional totals `reasoning_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens` and
`cost` are left out when their sum is zero. A local model that reports
no cost leaves `cost` out of the result.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/msgs.py#L308"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### sum_usage

``` python
def sum_usage(
    us
):
```

*Add up OpenAI usage dicts, skipping None and keeping the first `model`
named.*

``` python
test_eq(sum_usage([{'total_tokens': 3}, None, {'total_tokens': 4, 'model': 'gpt-5.1'}]),
        {'prompt_tokens': 0, 'completion_tokens': 0, 'total_tokens': 7,
         'cached_tokens': 0, 'model': 'gpt-5.1'})
test_eq(sum_usage([]), None)
test_eq(sum_usage([None]), None)
test_eq('cost' in sum_usage([{'cost': 0.0}]), False)
test_eq(sum_usage([{'cost': 0.5}])['cost'], 0.5)
```

## Prompt transports

Some backends take one block of text instead of a list of messages.
These backends have no tokenizer of their own. A tokenizer splits text
into tokens, the units that a model counts.

`est_tokens(text)` estimates the token count of `text`. It divides the
length by `CHARS_PER_TOKEN`, which is 3.25, and rounds up. It returns 0
for empty text.

`render_prompt(hist, sp)` writes a conversation as one block of text.
The block starts with the system prompt `sp`. Each message then gets a
heading and its text. A message with no text and no tool calls is
skipped. The table shows the headings.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Message role</th>
<th>Heading</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>user</code></td>
<td><code>## User</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>assistant</code></td>
<td><code>## Assistant</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>system</code></td>
<td><code>## System</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>tool</code></td>
<td><code>## Tool result (name)</code>, with the tool name in the
brackets</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A tool call is written as a `tool_call` block with a JSON object that
has `name` and `arguments`. This is the form that
[`tag_tools_sp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/tags.html#tag_tools_sp)
teaches the model. The example renders a short conversation with one
tool call.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/msgs.py#L330"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    hist, sp:str=''

```

*Render a conversation as one block of text with a heading per message.*

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### est_tokens

``` python
def est_tokens(
    text

```

*Estimate the token count of `text` from its length.*

``` python
test_eq(est_tokens(''), 0)
test_eq(est_tokens('a'), 1)
test_eq(est_tokens('a' * 13), 4)
assert est_tokens('a' * 350) > 100   # above the measured 3.50 chars/token, never below
```

``` python
hist = [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'what is 1+1?'},
        {'role': 'assistant', 'content': '', 'tool_calls': [ToolCall('add', {'a': 1, 'b': 1})]},
        {'role': 'tool', 'name': 'add', 'content': '2'},
        {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'Two.'}]
print(render_prompt(hist, 'Be brief.'))
```

``` python
out = render_prompt(hist, 'Be brief.')
test_eq(out.split('\n\n')[0], 'Be brief.')
assert '## Tool result (add)' in out and '<tool_call>' in out
test_eq(render_prompt([{'role': 'user', 'content': ''}]), '')
```

## Prefix reuse

A local engine keeps a KV cache. The KV cache holds the model state for
the tokens that the engine has already processed. When a new prompt
starts with the same tokens as the last prompt, the engine reuses that
part of the cache and processes only the new tokens.
`common_prefix_len(a, b)` returns the number of leading items that two
token lists share. This number is the count of tokens that a backend can
reuse.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/urai/blob/main/urai/msgs.py#L345"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### common_prefix_len

``` python
def common_prefix_len(
    a, b
):
```

*Length of the longest common prefix of sequences `a` and `b`.*

``` python
test_eq(common_prefix_len([1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 2, 9]), 2)
test_eq(common_prefix_len([1, 2], [1, 2]), 2)
test_eq(common_prefix_len([], [1]), 0)
test_eq(common_prefix_len([9], [1]), 0)
```
